title: Slipping out Saturday nights to the club; Uncle Charlie doubts him
summary: He went to the club where his uncle worked, said he would ask the band to let him sing, and was told they wouldn't allow it.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So after I got out of runnin' the back boys up there, I got so I say, well, my Uncle Charlie was still workin' in the nightclub. So I decided, I say, "Well, I gonna take up where I left off at. I'm gonna go to try to get back in them joints and sing some. So I used to put on ...Saturday night I'd take one little bath and everything, and...
Momma ask, "Where you goin'?" Say, "I'm goin' to a party. Some of the kids havin' a birth-day party."
So we go to the party. Party break up about ten...twelve o'clock. So's...everybody hadda go to bed. Me, I didn't go to bed.
I say, "I'm goin' out to see my uncle." So I would go back down to the nightclub, hang around the door with him, watchin' all the pretty girls come in an' all the hipcats, havin' a ball.
So, finally, I told my uncle...I say, "I'm gonna go up to the band and ask 'em let me sing a song or two."
He didn't know I could sing at all. He told me...said, "They ain't gonna let you sing. You can't have nobody messin' up. This ain't no play place. You can't go up there and goof off."
So I said, "I ain't gonna goof. I'm gonna sing."
So, say, "They ain't gonna let you."
